column3: The Hebrew names strength of heart; BSB says strength of understanding.
The Hebrew first names the righteous one in the singular, then says they are exalted; BSB describes God exalting them.
The Hebrew separately names their deeds and transgressions, then says they behaved proudly; BSB combines this as arrogant transgression.
The Hebrew has a singular ear; BSB has ears.
The Hebrew separately names their soul and their life; BSB says they die.
The Hebrew leaves God unnamed in this verse; BSB explicitly names God.
The Hebrew explicitly describes a broad place without constraint; BSB describes a spacious and broad place.
The Hebrew names rage and a ransom; BSB describes someone enticing him with riches and a large bribe.
The Hebrew has peoples in the plural and their place; BSB says people and homes.
The Hebrew does not explicitly repeat to Him before the quoted accusation; BSB supplies it.
The Hebrew says we do not know; BSB describes being beyond our knowledge.
The Hebrew names light and the roots of the sea; BSB says lightning and depths.
